title: A project of the thermal triple axis spectrometer at the PIK reactor
authors: Maria Iuzviuk, Nikita Kovalenko, Vladislav Tolichev, Aleksandr Ovsianikov, Oleg Usmanov, Anna Matveeva, Igor Zobkalo, Vladislav Tarnavich
abstract: A project of the novel thermal triple axis spectrometer IN1 at the PIK reactor is presented. Monte Carlo simulations were used for optimization its main parameters. The optimization of the instrument gives an estimated neutron flux as high as 109 n/cm2/s at the sample position at neutron energy about 36 meV at the designed 100 MW power. The modelling of neutron stages like monochromators, analyzers, virtual source, as well as instrument shielding was fulfilled to obtain the best performance of the spectrometer.
summary: This paper details the engineering and simulation project for a new thermal triple-axis spectrometer (IN1) to be installed at the PIK reactor. Using Monte Carlo simulations, the authors optimized the instrument's components, including virtual sources and monochromators, to achieve high neutron flux. The work also thoroughly models the necessary radiation shielding to ensure safe operation during inelastic neutron scattering experiments.
main_problem: The paper presents the design and optimization of a novel thermal triple-axis spectrometer (IN1) for use at the PIK reactor.
main_result: Monte Carlo simulations estimate a high neutron flux of up to $10^9 	ext{ n/cm}^2/	ext{s}$ at the sample position, and the design details extensive shielding to ensure safe operation.
method: The study heavily relies on Monte Carlo (MC) simulations (using McStas and PHITS) to optimize instrument parameters, model neutron transport, and calculate radiation dose distributions.
model_or_system: The physical system is the IN1 spectrometer, which utilizes the Rowland geometry at the PIK reactor. Key components include virtual sources, monochromators (HOPG, Ge, Si), and analyzers, all optimized via simulation.
key_observables: Neutron flux density at the sample position, background radiation levels, and the equivalent dose rate (DER) in the surrounding facility area.
important_parameters: Neutron energy range ($15 	ext{ meV} < E_i < 100 	ext{ meV}$), designed reactor power ($100 	ext{ MW}$), and optimal crystal/source dimensions.
main_assumptions: The design assumes the successful operation of the PIK reactor at high power and relies on the use of virtual source concepts to maintain geometric accuracy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectrometer's 3D model, the neutron spectrum, the beam profile, and detailed simulations of the neutron and gamma-ray dose rate distribution within the complex shielding structure.
paper_structure: The paper details the scientific problem, presents the IN1 design, describes the simulation methodology (MC modeling of components and shielding), and reports the optimized parameters and expected performance metrics.
why_interesting: While focused on reactor instrumentation, the rigorous application of advanced simulation techniques (MC) to model complex radiation transport and optimize experimental setups is highly relevant to any experimental quantum physics facility.
